speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These include the International Convention against the Taking of Hostages and the International Convention for the Suppression of Terrorist Bombings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
text: As a responsible and effective member of the international community, we are committed to facilitating greater international cooperation to combat transnational crime, in accordance with our domestic laws and international obligations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Both countries must find it mutually beneficial to enter into such an arrangement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Sometimes, these arrangements are easier to Page: 44 conclude when countries come from the same legal traditions and have very similar legal systems and procedures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Where there is greater divergence in the respective legal systems and procedures, the differences will need to be rationalised or a consensus reached as to the legal procedures to be applied before an arrangement can be concluded.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, it has led many people to ask: what if there are more foreigners who come here and commit crime and then run to Thailand?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, it is something that is being looked at, a sort of framework that member countries can tap on should it turn out that the circumstances and conditions are right for them to enter into bilateral arrangements.
